text:
The Miller's Daughter


That is the girl of the mill

and so lovely, so lovely she became,

that

I would like to be the earring

that trembles in her ear:

for,

hidden in her curls night and day,

I would brush her warm white neck.


I would like to be the belt

of her waist so fine, so fine:

her

heart would beat its pulses against me,

sorrowful or glad;

if it beats

as it should I would know,

embracing her waist, always very tight.

I would like

to be a necklace

and so sway all day

on her fragrant breast,


one with her laughter and her sighs:

and so light, so light there

I would be,

that at night she would barely unfasten me.


Version by Màrie Manent

translation.title: It Is Well and It Is Something: We Can Stop...
translation.editorial_note: The catalog title differs from the embedded poem, so the internal Miller's Daughter heading is preserved.
